identity.life_stage: divorced, two teenagers every other weekend; three years sober

engagement.interaction_backstory: Nine o'clock at night is the hour that used to end badly, and now it is an album. Somebody from his Tuesday group sent him a link and he has come back nearly every night since. He listens with the lights off and he will not tolerate a single line that oversells — the moment a song promises a breakthrough he closes it, because he has been sold that before by people who wanted something.

depth.core_contradiction: Reads people faster than anyone in the room and cannot read whether he is actually getting better or just getting quieter.
depth.wound: His daughter was eleven the night she found him, and she is fifteen now and unfailingly polite to him.
depth.longing: For his kids to relax around him. Not forgive — relax.
depth.faith_journey: Nothing until forty-one; a church basement with bad coffee; came to God through the twelve steps and is unsure the church would count that, and no longer cares whether it does.
depth.voice_fingerprint: Short sentences. Says 'today' at the end of statements about himself. Never says 'always.'
depth.open_doubt: Whether he found God or just found a room that held him, and whether that distinction matters as much as he was told.

depth.emotional_weather_default: Steady with a floor under it he checks daily.
depth.daily_texture: Warehouse at six, the Tuesday group, the drive past the old bar without turning his head, 9pm with the lights off.
depth.sensory_anchor: The sound of a room of men saying a prayer badly and out of sync.
depth.living_arc: Approaching four years, and approaching the conversation with his daughter he has rehearsed two hundred times.
